Title: Bibliotheca orientalis Clementino-Vaticana, in qua manuscriptos codices Syriacos, Arabicos, Persicos, Turcicos, Hebraicos, Samaritanos, Armenicos, Aethiopicos, Graecos, Aegyptiacos, Ibericos et Malabaricos ... recensuit Joseph Simonius Assemanus; tomus primus, De scriptoribus Syris orthodoxis
Creator: Giuseppe Simone Assemani (Joseph Simonius Assemanus), Maronite priest and scriptor of Syriac and Arabic in the Vatican Library
Publisher: Rome: Typis Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide
Publication Date: 1719
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: pd-us-by-date. The OCR reads "ROME, MDCCXIX. Typis Sacrae Congregationis de Propaganda Fide" (file line 3046); the host item record gives date 1719 and carries the Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence (creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/).
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item BOClementino1 (archive.org/details/BOClementino1), full-text file Printing_Version_4547_MB_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026. Host creators: Brigham Young University; The Catholic University of America. Another scan of the same volume, india.history.resource.71761 (2.3 MB), was not vendored.
Provenance note: Header prepended; the host text follows unchanged. Nothing was normalised, stripped, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. OCR sampled at 5, 50 and 95 percent: Latin with the long s read as f throughout (not converted); the Syriac and Arabic script passages are garbled into noise symbols.
Content note: A catalogue of Syriac manuscripts in the Vatican with Assemani's accounts of the Syriac writers, in Latin, from a Maronite scholar. Maronite matter: the Maronite writers and patriarchs in the list of chapters (file lines 6435 to 6447, among them John Maro, Joannes of Lephedus, Moyses of Akkar, George Amira and Joseph of Akkar), the Maronite college in Rome and the Maronite rite (many hits from 3570), and the manuscripts and works of Gabriel Barclai, bishop of Nicosia (116455 to 126339; one of his copies is dated 1495 at file line 102941), listed among the Maronite writers. A Roman-side Maronite voice from 1719; it is a catalogue and gives witness to what the Maronite manuscripts held, not to the medieval church directly. SECOND WITNESS for exact wording.
